package_info.package_versions: Version notarized and distributed during the 3CX supply chain attack (exact version not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was trojanized to include malicious components, enabling supply chain compromise. Despite being notarized by Apple, it contained code designed to execute unauthorized actions on user systems, demonstrating that even trusted distribution channels can be subverted.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Trojanized installer component (reverse engineered by Patrick Wardle, specific code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely Objective-C or Swift, as per macOS app development)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At installation and runtime, the code executes additional payloads embedded within the installer, establishes network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure, and may exfiltrate sensitive data or download further malicious modules.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The installer contains unauthorized code that is not part of the legitimate 3CX application, designed to execute post-installation and communicate with external servers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal installers should only install and configure the legitimate application. The presence of hidden payloads and network activity unrelated to app functionality is a clear violation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate updaters may contact vendor servers for updates, but not unknown or untrusted domains, nor execute hidden payloads.
key_indicators: Presence of hidden or obfuscated code in installer
Execution of code not present in official source

attack_chain.action: User downloads and installs the trojanized 3CX Desktop App from a trusted source (App Store or official site).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code embedded in the installer is executed.

attack_chain.action: Malicious payload establishes network connections to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential exfiltration of data or download of additional malware.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains persistence or further control over the compromised system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: system compromise, data theft, or lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Installer or application making unexpected outbound network connections
Execution of code not present in official source repositories
Presence of obfuscated or hidden payloads in installer packages
file_indicators: Trojanized 3CX Desktop App installer (hashes and filenames as per threat intelligence feeds)
Unexpected binaries or scripts within application bundle
network_indicators: Connections to known attacker-controlled domains or IPs associated with 3CX attack
Outbound traffic immediately after installation to untrusted endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for application installers and updates that contain code not present in official sources. Use behavioral analysis to detect installers or applications that make unexpected network connections or execute hidden payloads. Compare package contents using differential analysis to identify unauthorized changes. Correlate with threat intelligence on known malicious domains and file hashes.
